descripcion_es: Paying, banking, buying, exchanging and returning products.
resumen: Vocabulary and phrases for paying, talking about prices, doing simple banking and complaining about or returning a purchase.

explicacion.texto: Several money verbs take fixed prepositions: pay for something (es: pagar algo), spend money on something (es: gastar en algo), borrow from (es: pedir prestado a), lend to (es: prestar a). Money is uncountable: much money, not many moneys.

filas: give money in exchange for something (es: pagar algo)
I paid for the tickets online.
pay with notes and coins / with a card (es: pagar en efectivo / con tarjeta)
use money to buy things (es: gastar dinero en)
She spends a lot on clothes.
low in price / high in price (es: barato / caro)
have enough money for something (es: permitirse económicamente)
We can't afford a new car.
take something you will give back / give something someone will give back (es: pedir prestado / prestar)
Can you lend me ten euros?
have to pay money back to someone (es: deber dinero)
money you get back when you pay too much (es: cambio, vuelta)
a piece of paper that proves you paid (es: tique, recibo)
a reduction in price / a period of lower prices (es: descuento / rebajas)
There's a 20% discount in the sales.
an arrangement to keep money in a bank (es: cuenta bancaria)
a machine in the street that gives out money (es: cajero automático)
Is there a cash machine near here?
take money out of your account (es: sacar dinero)
a card to pay now and settle later / a card that takes money directly from your account (es: tarjeta de crédito / débito)
a secret number for your card (es: número secreto)
return something to the shop (es: devolver algo a la tienda)
money given back to you (es: reembolso)
swap for another product (es: cambiar por otro producto)
Can I exchange this for a bigger size?
put on clothes to see if they are right (es: probarse ropa)
It is not the right size / it does not look good on me (es: no me queda bien de talla / no me favorece)

items: Receipt is the proof of purchase (es: tique); recipe is a set of cooking instructions (es: receta de cocina).
Fit refers to size; suit, to whether it looks good on you.
Borrow: I receive; lend: I give. I borrowed a book from Ana = Ana lent me a book.

ejemplos.frase: Can I pay by card, or do you only take cash?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta o solo aceptan efectivo?

ejemplos.frase: We spend too much money on takeaways.
ejemplos.traduccion: Gastamos demasiado dinero en comida para llevar.

ejemplos.frase: I can't afford to go on holiday this year.
ejemplos.traduccion: Este año no me puedo permitir irme de vacaciones.

ejemplos.frase: Could you lend me your umbrella?
These jeans don't fit me. Can I exchange them?
ejemplos.traduccion: Estos vaqueros no me valen. ¿Puedo cambiarlos?

ejemplos.frase: Without the receipt we can't give you a refund.
ejemplos.traduccion: Sin el tique no podemos devolverle el dinero.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: To pay for a thing is pay for; pay the bill/rent has no for.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Can you borrow me your pen?
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Can you lend me your pen?
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: To give something to someone for a time is lend; borrow means to take something you will give back (es: pedir prestado).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I spend a lot of money in books.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I spend a lot of money on books.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Can I have the recipe, please? (en una tienda)
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Can I have the receipt, please?
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The proof of purchase (es: tique) is a receipt.

ejercicios.frase: How much did you pay ___ that jacket?
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that paying for a thing is pay for something. The clue is that jacket, the object bought. In English, without for, the object of pay is the person or the bill (pay the waiter, pay the bill), not what is bought.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To pay for something is pay for something.

errores_previstos.explicacion: By indicates the means of payment (by card); the object bought goes with for.
Pay to would be used for the person who receives the money, not for what is bought.

ejercicios.frase: He spends all his money ___ video games.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes spend (money) on (es: gastar dinero en). The clue is spends all his money, followed by what it is spent on. The fixed preposition is on, not in as in Spanish.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se gasta todo el dinero en videojuegos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “gastar en”: in English we say spend on.
For goes with pay (pay for); with spend, on.

ejercicios.explicacion: The second table in the card gives try on (es: probarse ropa). It is a phrasal verb: try alone means to attempt or to taste something, and on adds the idea of putting it on. The clue is trousers, an item of clothing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To put on clothes to check them is try on.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Try in does not exist; to put on clothes to check them is try on.
Try out means to test something to see if it works (a car, a method), not to try on clothes.

ejercicios.frase: Thanks for paying. I ___ you fifteen euros.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes owe (es: deber dinero). The clue is Thanks for paying: the other person paid for me, so now I have a debt with him. Owe is followed by the person and the amount: I owe you fifteen euros.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To have a debt is owe.
ejercicios.traduccion: Gracias por pagar. Te debo quince euros.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Must expresses obligation (es: deber hacer algo); having a debt (es: deber dinero) is owe.
Have to means having to do something, and would need a verb after it; having a debt is owe.

ejercicios.frase: Could you ___ me some money until Friday?
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes lend (I give) from borrow (I receive). In Could you ___ me, the person who gives the money is you, so the verb is lend: lend me (es: préstame). The clue is me after the gap: the person who receives is the object.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Lend me (es: préstame): you give the money; I receive it.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Me podrías prestar algo de dinero hasta el viernes?

por_opcion.lend: Correct: lend someone something = give something to someone for a time (es: prestar algo a alguien).
por_opcion.borrow: Incorrect: borrow means to take something you will give back and does not take the receiver as its object; borrow me is a typical mistake.
por_opcion.owe: Incorrect: owe means to have a debt, not to lend money.

ejercicios.frase: Can I ___ your car this weekend?
ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, borrow = take something you will give back (es: pedir prestado): the subject is the receiver. In Can I ___ your car, the person who receives the car is me, so the verb is borrow. The natural Spanish translation is “¿me dejas…?”, but in English the point of view is that of the borrower.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Me puedes dejar tu coche este fin de semana?

por_opcion.borrow: Correct: Can I borrow…? = may I take … and give it back later? (es: ¿puedo tomar prestado…?)
por_opcion.lend: Incorrect: with I as the subject, lend would mean that I lend the car, which is not mine.
por_opcion.rent me: Incorrect: rent means to pay to use something, and rent me with I as the subject makes no sense.

ejercicios.frase: It's a beautiful flat, but we can't ___ it.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives afford (es: permitirse económicamente), which almost always appears with can or can't. The clue is but we can't…: the problem is the price. Afford is transitive: can't afford it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To have enough money for something is afford.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es un piso precioso, pero no nos lo podemos permitir.

por_opcion.afford: Correct: can't afford = not have enough money for something (es: no poder permitirse).
por_opcion.pay: Incorrect: can't pay it would mean “I can't pay it” to someone; for the object bought you would say pay for.
por_opcion.spend: Incorrect: spend needs the amount and on (spend money on); it does not express the idea of affording something.

ejercicios.frase: This dress is the right size, but the colour doesn't ___ me.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes fit (size) from suit (whether it looks good on you). The clue is the sentence itself: the right size says the size is fine, and the problem is the colour, a question of style. That is why it is doesn't suit me.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If it is a question of style or colour, suit; fit is about size.
ejercicios.traduccion: Este vestido es de mi talla, pero el color no me favorece.

por_opcion.suit: Correct: suit = look good on someone because of style or colour (es: favorecer, sentar bien).
por_opcion.fit: Incorrect: fit is about size, and the sentence says the size is right.
por_opcion.match: Incorrect: match means to go well with something else (The bag matches the shoes), not to look good on a person.

ejercicios.frase: My brother borrowed me his bike.
respuestas: My brother lent me his bike.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card reminds you that borrow is receiving and lend is giving. Here my brother gives the bike and I receive it, so the verb is lend. Lend is irregular: the past is lent.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To give something to someone for a time is lend (lent).
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermano me prestó su bici.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My brother borrowed me his bike.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: borrow does not take the receiver as its object.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My brother lended me his bike.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Lend is irregular: the past is lent.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My brother lent his bike me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: If the thing comes first, the person takes to (lent his bike to me); the normal form is lent me his bike.

ejercicios.frase: Please keep the recipe in case you want to return it.
respuestas: Please keep the receipt in case you want to return it.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that receipt is the proof of purchase (es: tique, recibo de compra), and recipe is a set of cooking instructions (es: receta de cocina). The clue is in case you want to return it: you need the proof of purchase. Watch the pronunciation: in receipt the p is silent.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The proof of purchase is a receipt.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, guarde el tique por si quiere devolverlo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please keep the recipe in case you want to return it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: recipe means a set of cooking instructions.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please keep the ticket in case you want to return it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Ticket is an entry ticket or a travel ticket; the proof of purchase is a receipt.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Please keep the receit in case you want to return it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is spelt receipt, with a silent p.

ejercicios.frase: I paid the dinner with my credit card.
respuestas: I paid for the dinner with my credit card.
I paid for dinner with my credit card.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that paying for a thing is pay for something; without for the object would be the person or the bill (pay the bill). The clue is the dinner, what is being paid for. Both pay for the dinner and pay for dinner, without an article, are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To pay for something is pay for.
ejercicios.traduccion: Pagué la cena con mi tarjeta de crédito.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I paid the dinner with my credit card.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: for is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I paid for the dinner by my credit card.
errores_previstos.explicacion: We say by card, but with a possessive we use with: with my credit card.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives pay by card (es: pagar con tarjeta), with by and no article. Can I pay by card? is the typical question in a shop, with can before the subject. The statement I can pay by card is also accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition goes first: by card.
A calque of the order “¿puedo con tarjeta pagar?”: the verb goes before the complement.

ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes refund (es: reembolso), money given back to you. Get a refund is the usual collocation: getting your money back. The question has can before the subject, and the statement is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Refund is money given back to you.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb goes before the object: get a refund.
In the question the subject goes right after can: Can I get.

ejercicios.frase: I need to ___ some money from the cash machine.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives withdraw money (es: sacar dinero), which is somewhat formal; in speech people also say get money, take out money or draw out money (the last one somewhat more British and less frequent). The clue is from the cash machine. All four forms are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To take money out is withdraw (formal), get, take out or draw out.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tengo que sacar dinero del cajero.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “retirar”: retire means to stop working because of age; taking money out is withdraw, get or take out.
Withdrawal is the noun (the act of taking money out); after need to you need the verb withdraw.
A calque of Spanish “extraer”; it is not used for money from a cash machine.

ejercicios.frase: Here's a twenty-euro note. – Thank you. And here's your ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives change (es: cambio), the money you get back when you pay. It is uncountable in this sense: your change, with no plural. The clue is that the customer has paid with a note and the shop assistant gives him money back.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The money you get back is change.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aquí tiene un billete de veinte euros. Gracias, y aquí tiene su cambio.

por_opcion.change: Correct: change = the money you get back (es: la vuelta, el cambio).
por_opcion.rest: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “el resto”; rest means a break or what is left of something.
por_opcion.return: Incorrect: return is the return of a product or of a journey, not the money you get back when you pay.

descripcion_larga_es: Vocabulary and phrases for paying, talking about prices, doing simple banking and returning or exchanging a purchase. It is survival vocabulary for any trip or stay abroad. Spanish speakers find it hard because many verbs take fixed prepositions (pay for, spend on), because borrow and lend are both translated as “prestar” and because receipt and recipe are easily confused.

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary of money and shopping: verbs like pay, spend, cost, afford, save, borrow, lend and owe; banking words (account, cash machine, PIN) and shopping words (receipt, refund, exchange, try on, fit, suit).
contexto.por_que_importa: It is used in unavoidable everyday situations: paying, taking out money, asking for the receipt or returning something. A mistake like “borrow me” or “I paid the dinner” is understood, but it can cause confusion (who is lending to whom?) and it sounds unnatural. In basic-level exams it is a standard vocabulary area.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: In shops, restaurants, banks and among friends when lending each other money. The clues are the prepositions (for, on, by, in) and the direction of the loan. Spanish speakers tend to say “pay the tickets” for “pagar las entradas” and to use borrow for both meanings of “prestar”.
